  • Constructor Details

    • SimulationUI

      public SimulationUI(Scenario selectedScenario)
      Constructs a new SimulationUI instance based on the specified scenario. Initializes the selected scenario and retrieves the corresponding map from the repository. If the selected map is not found, an exception is thrown.
      Parameters:
      selectedScenario - the scenario to be used for the simulation; must not be null
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the provided scenario is null or if the map for the scenario cannot be found

  • Method Details

    • start

      public void start() throws Exception
      Starts the simulation UI by creating a new instance of the JavaFX Stage. This method is an entry point that delegates to the overloaded start method responsible for initializing and displaying the application stage.
      Throws:
      Exception - if an error occurs during the initialization or loading of UI components

    • start

      public void start(javafx.stage.Stage stage) throws Exception
      Initializes and displays the main stage for the railway simulation application. This method sets up the JavaFX user interface, including loading FXML resources, creating controllers, and configuring the primary stage. The method initializes the simulation and assigns the necessary components to the controller. It sets up the primary scene, configures the stage properties, and handles the application close request to ensure proper cleanup of resources. Additionally, this method starts simulation threads once the UI is fully configured.
      Parameters:
      stage - the primary stage for the JavaFX application, provided by the platform; must not be null
      Throws:
      Exception - if an error occurs during initialization or while loading FXML resources

    • requestUIUpdate

      public void requestUIUpdate()
      Requests an update of the user interface by invoking the corresponding method on the associated controller, if it exists. This method acts as a delegate to ensure that any necessary UI changes are properly handled through the controller. This method is typically used to propagate updates in response to changes within the simulation or application state, ensuring the user interface reflects the most up-to-date information. If the controller is not set, calling this method will have no effect. Thread-Safety: This method may be safely called from any thread, as the underlying controller's implementation ensures proper handling of UI updates.

    • pauseGame

      public void pauseGame()
      Pauses the current simulation by setting the running state to false. This method ensures that any ongoing simulation processes are halted, and prints a notification to the console indicating the paused state. Thread-Safety: This method is thread-safe as it uses an AtomicBoolean to manage the running state. Side Effects: - Updates the `running` field to false.

    • resumeGame

      public void resumeGame()
      Resumes the current simulation by setting the running state to true. This method ensures that any previously paused simulation processes are restarted, and prints a notification to the console indicating the resumed state. Thread-Safety: This method is thread-safe as it utilizes an AtomicBoolean to manage the running state. Side Effects: - Updates the `running` field to true.

    • stopSimulation

      public void stopSimulation()
      Stops the current simulation, ensuring proper cleanup of resources, saving the simulation state, and resetting game data if necessary. This method handles the following tasks: - Marks the simulation as no longer running by updating the `running` state to false. - Shuts down all active schedulers (Time, Generation, and Route) with a controlled timeout to avoid resource leaks or unexpected behavior. - Attempts to save the current simulation state using the associated controller, including the map, scenario, current year, and user budget. - If the game-over condition is met, performs a game reset by clearing user-related data (such as locomotives and stations) and reinitializing the game parameters. - Saves the game state to a file using a separate utility. - Logs any errors encountered during the saving or resetting process for troubleshooting purposes. - Sets the simulation object to null to indicate it is no longer active. Thread-Safety: This method should be used in a controlled environment where no concurrent modifications are performed on the simulation state or related objects while this method is executing. Side Effects: - Updates the `running` state to false. - Performs I/O operations, including saving the simulation state to persistent storage. - Resets user game data in case of a game-over condition. - Outputs information and error messages to the console for debugging.

    • getSimulation

      public Simulation getSimulation()
      Retrieves the current simulation instance associated with the SimulationUI. This method provides access to the `Simulation` object that represents the core of the railway simulation. It can be used to interact with or query the simulation state, such as retrieving details about the active map, scenario, or simulation parameters.
      Returns:
      the current `Simulation` instance if initialized; otherwise, null.

      Retrieves the current simulation controller associated with the SimulationUI. This method provides access to the `SimulationController` that is responsible for managing the logic and interactions within the simulation. The controller serves as a central point for controlling simulation behavior and facilitating communication between the UI and simulation core.
      Returns:

    • getSelectedScenario

      public Scenario getSelectedScenario()
      Retrieves the currently selected simulation scenario. This method returns the `Scenario` object that represents the active scenario being used in the simulation. The selected scenario is typically initialized during the construction of the `SimulationUI` instance and may determine the configurations, rules, and environment the simulation operates under.
      Returns:
      the currently selected `Scenario` if one has been set; otherwise, null.

    • getSelectedMap

This method provides access to the `Map` object that has been chosen for the simulation, allowing interaction with map-specific data or configurations. The selected map is typically initialized based on the scenario selection during the SimulationUI's setup phase.
      Returns:
